ai_summary: Scottish wind generation currently stands at an estimated 2.9 GW, representing 28.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity, while total GB wind output reaches 13.6 GW. This substantial volume of renewable generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to an exceptional 2 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide average of 72 gCO2/kWh. However, persistent cross-border transmission bottlenecks prevent this clean power from flowing south into major demand centres, resulting in extensive network curtailment. So far today, 7,462 MWh of Scottish generation has been turned down through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £431,133. To replace this lost energy and maintain system balance, an estimated 1,417,837 m3 of gas had to be burned elsewhere, emitting an additional 2,612 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Extrapolating today’s constraint expenditure across the entire year yields an estimated total yearly cost of £157 million. Distributed across annual national demand, this constraint run-rate represents an estimated increase of roughly £0.55/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the severe environmental and financial penalties imposed by current grid infrastructure bottlenecks.
